C1.rationale: Level 2 anchor is satisfied: assessed collaborative practice recurs systematically across every single accounting and management core subject with individual exam accountability and group presentations. In ACCT90002 Financial Statement Analysis, students collaborate in groups of 4–5 on a 4000-word financial analysis report; in ACCT90010 Strategic Performance Management, teams of 4–5 complete a 5000-word strategic assignment; in ACCT90012 Corporate Reporting, groups deliver a 5000-word corporate reporting report; and in ACCT90014 Auditing, teams deliver a 5000-word assurance project. Level 3 is not met: while teams use modern accounting and spreadsheet tools, formal assessed role-and-tool allocation charters dividing work between human accountants and autonomous AI audit/financial modeling agents are unevidenced.

C2.rationale: Level 2 anchor is satisfied: core assessment includes criterion-referenced appraisal of financial statements, corporate reporting disclosures, audit risks, and strategic cost allocations in complex business case studies. In ACCT90002, students critically evaluate corporate financial performance and earnings quality; in ACCT90014, students evaluate internal controls and audit risk evidence; and in ACCT90013, students appraise financial accounting theories and standard-setting choices. Level 3 is not met: no core assessment requires students to document and justify reliance decisions regarding AI-driven audit or tax reconciliation tools, defend judgements of AI financial analysis outputs, or evidence systematic override logs over time.

C3.rationale: Level 2 anchor is satisfied: core units directly address accounting information systems, internal control frameworks, database structures, quantitative modeling, and IT audit constraints. In ACCT90030 Information Processes & Control, students analyze accounting system architecture, data flows, and internal control frameworks with assessed presentations and assignments; in ECOM90009 Quantitative Methods for Business, students complete quantitative modeling tasks. Level 3 is not met: systemic critique of AI governance in corporate financial reporting, algorithmic audit bias, regulatory data protection (APRA/ASIC), or statutory tax AI governance is not formally assessed in the core.

C4.rationale: Level 2 anchor is satisfied: core assessment requires transfer of financial accounting, management accounting, taxation, auditing, and corporate law frameworks across diverse commercial contexts and entity types (from multinational corporate groups in ACCT90012 to assurance engagements in ACCT90014 and tax planning in ACCT90016). Level 3 is not met: the program does not mandate a universal self-scoped research project or assessed identification of one's own accounting capability gaps with an explicit closure plan across every graduation pathway.

C5.rationale: Level 2 anchor is satisfied: students design and conduct secondary and empirical financial investigations, analyzing corporate annual reports, auditing internal controls, and testing forensic accounting evidence against regulatory standards in ACCT90002, ACCT90012, ACCT90014, and ACCT90015. Level 3 is not met: no universal mandatory primary-evidence thesis with oral viva defense before an external examination panel is required across the core.

W1.rationale: Level 2 anchor is satisfied: core assessment requires recognised professional accounting genres judged against statutory accounting standards (AASB/IFRS) and professional criteria (CPA/CAANZ). In ACCT90002, students author formal Financial Statement Analysis Reports; in ACCT90014, students produce comprehensive Audit Opinions and Working Papers; in ACCT90016, students author formal Tax Advice Memos; and in ACCT90030, students deliver Accounting Information Control Presentations. Level 3 is not met: presentations and reports in core accounting units are evaluated internally by academic faculty without documented compulsory external audit partner or client panels.

W2.rationale: Level 2 anchor is satisfied: core assessment reproduces professional accounting, auditing, and financial reporting tasks end-to-end (complex journal entries, group consolidation, materiality threshold testing, audit risk matrix construction, and tax planning in ACCT90002, ACCT90012, ACCT90014, ACCT90016).
